# Documentation Guidelines

## Code Documentation

- Use JSDoc comments for functions and classes
- Document function parameters and return values
- Explain complex algorithms or business logic
- Document assumptions and constraints
- Keep comments up to date with code changes
- Avoid obvious comments that don't add value

## API Documentation

- Document all API endpoints
- Include HTTP method, path, and description
- Document request parameters and body
- Document response format and status codes
- Provide example requests and responses
- Document authentication requirements

## README Documentation

- Provide clear project overview
- Include installation instructions
- Document environment variables
- Provide usage examples
- Include troubleshooting section
- Document deployment process

## Inline Comments

- Explain "why" not "what"
- Use comments for complex business logic
- Document workarounds and temporary solutions
- Mark TODOs with clear descriptions
- Use consistent comment style

## Function Documentation

- Use JSDoc format for consistency
- Document all parameters with types
- Document return values
- Document thrown exceptions
- Include usage examples for complex functions

## Module Documentation

- Provide module-level overview
- Document public API
- Explain module dependencies
- Document configuration options
- Include examples of module usage

## Configuration Documentation

- Document all environment variables
- Provide example configuration files
- Explain configuration options
- Document default values
- Include security considerations

## Changelog

- Maintain a changelog for significant changes
- Follow semantic versioning
- Document breaking changes
- Include migration guides when necessary
- Date all entries

## Best Practices

- Keep documentation close to code
- Update documentation with code changes
- Review documentation during code review
- Use clear and concise language
- Include diagrams for complex flows
- Keep documentation version-controlled
